title: Idempotent WS frame accounting across reconnects and regional failover
creator: Evelyn Chen
description: Investigate and implement an idempotent accounting approach for partially delivered or truncated websocket frames to prevent double-counting or missed token charges when clients reconnect, experience regional failover, or when the gateway retries. Current pipeline can attribute bytes/tokens twice or drop them when frame boundaries and ACKs are ambiguous across connection boundaries.
acceptance_criteria: Metering events for a logical session must be identical whether delivered via a single long-lived WS or across N reconnects (deterministic checksum / ordered-aggregation).
No customer should see >0.01% change in billed tokens for replayed reconnection test traffic versus baseline single-connection test traffic.
Edge-case reproducer suite (see related PR) added to CI that simulates partial frames, duplicate-delivery, delayed ACKs, and region-switch reconnects.
Rollout gated by shadow meter validation showing parity within 0.1% for 72h in dedicated infra cluster.
notes: Root cause: gateway assigned provisional session offsets but upstream may resend final fragments without the gateway detecting dedupe keys when sequence numbers reset on reconnect.
Proposal: use an envelope-level id (session_id + stream_epoch + frame_offset) and maintain a short-lived dedupe table with range tombstones; emit idempotent metering deltas only on finalized frames.

Trade-offs: additional Redis/etcd lookups for dedupe on high-QPS paths vs. slightly delayed final accounting. We considered probabilistic dedupe (Bloom filter) but rejected due to billing precision requirements.
Alternative: move finalization responsibility to the client (client ACKs) — not feasible for older SDKs and 3rd-party users.
implementation_plan: 1) Add envelope id generation in gateway (session_id + reconnect_epoch + byte_offset).
2) Persist lightweight dedupe ranges in local LRU cache + authoritative compact store (etcd) for cross-instance reconcilations.
3) Update accounting pipeline to accept idempotent deltas; ignore duplicates based on stored ranges.
4) Add CI reproducer tests and a chaos job that kills connections mid-frame.
5) Shadow rollout in staging -> dedicated infra cluster -> gradual prod rollout (5% -> 25% -> 100%).
testing_plan: Unit tests for envelope id generation and range merge logic.
Integration tests against local dedupe store for cross-instance reconnection scenarios.
E2E load test: 50k WS sessions with randomized disconnects; measure billed tokens parity.
Shadow-metric comparison against current pipeline for 72h in staging and dedicated infra.
